title: Cuspy dark matter density profiles in massive dwarf galaxies
question: What is the inner slope of the dark matter density profile (β*) in six nearby spiral dwarf galaxies, and how does it compare with lower-mass dwarfs and cosmological hydrodynamical simulations?

data.sensitivity: 3.4-4.7 mJy beam^-1 (46-65 mK) per 2 km s^-1 channel

what.value: Tully-Fisher distances for three galaxies (NGC 1035, NGC 4451, NGC 6106)

evidence.quote: Three of our galaxies have Tully-Fisher distances reported by (cite: tully13).

what.value: Distances (`modbest` column) and morphological information from the HyperLEDA catalogue

evidence.quote: For the other three, we use the distances from the `modbest` column in the HyperLEDA catalogue (cite: makarov14)
All morphological information is taken from the HyperLEDA catalogue.

what.value: Initial kinematic parameters (centre, position angle, inclination, systemic velocity) and CARMA CO data

evidence.quote: The initial values for the kinematic parameters (centre, position angle, inclination, systemic velocity) were taken from (cite: truong17), but were adjusted by hand as needed.
Lower-sensitivity CARMA data of these galaxies taken in the C, D, and E configurations (antenna spacings from $7.5-373$ m) recover scales up to $\sim$ 40$\ensuremath{''}$ (cite: truong17).

what.value: Mass-to-light ratios (Υ*), atomic and molecular gas mass components, Hα rotation curves, stellar velocity curves, and literature β* values for overlapping galaxies

evidence.quote: This work closely follows that of (cite: relatores19a; relatores19b), who measured $\beta^*$ from another DGDM survey sub-sample using H $\alpha$ observations to trace the total potential.
To convert to mass, we assume a constant mass-to-light ratio ($\Upsilon_\star$) from stellar population synthesis models reported by (see their Table 1).
For the four galaxies that overlap with , we also include contributions from the atomic and molecular gas in the decomposition.

what.value: IRAC Channel 2 zero-point and absolute magnitude of the Sun at 4.5 μm

evidence.quote: To convert to solar luminosities, we find the luminosity of the Sun at 4.5 $\mu$m using the IRAC Channel 2 zero-point (cite: reach05) and the absolute magnitude of the Sun at 4.5 $\mu$m (cite: oh08).

what.value: Absolute magnitude of the Sun in SDSS r-band and effective central wavelength of the PS1 r-band filter

evidence.quote: The absolute magnitude of the Sun is 4.65 AB magnitudes in the SDSS $r$-band (cite: willmer18), and the effective central wavelength of the PS1 $r$-band filter is 617 nm (cite: tonry12).

what.value: Local Universe value of H0 = 73.2 km s^-1 Mpc^-1

evidence.loc: Measuring the inner slope of the dark matter density profile
evidence.quote: Assuming a local Universe value of $H_0 = 73.2 {\rm\ km\ s^{-1}\ Mpc^{-1}}$ (cite: riess21; divalentino21) yields $\rho_{\rm crit}=148.7{\rm\ M_\odot~kpc^{-3}}$.

what.value: Literature inner dark matter density slopes and mass models for comparison

evidence.quote: There is no overlap between our sample of galaxies and those from (cite: simon05), (cite: oh11; oh15), (cite: adams14), (cite: li19), or (cite: leung21).

external_data.citation: (cite: simon05), (cite: oh11; oh15), (cite: adams14), (cite: li19), (cite: leung21), (cite: lelli16)

recipe.goal: Image ALMA CO(1-0) data cubes and generate moment and error maps
recipe.method: Clean 3D RA-Dec-velocity cubes to the rms noise level, convolve to a circular beam, and fit each pixel spectrum with a Gaussian to produce peak intensity, velocity, and linewidth maps plus error maps; blank non-converging fits, interpolate isolated blanked pixels with neighbour median, and mask pixels with SNR < 3.
key_parameters: velocity resolution = 2 km s^-1, SNR >= 3 mask, minimum velocity uncertainty = 6 km s^-1
assumptions: Minimum velocity uncertainty of 6 km s^-1 accounts for random ISM motions (~1/3 of typical CO linewidth)

recipe.goal: Derive CO rotation curves and geometric parameters
recipe.method: First-order harmonic decomposition in concentric rings fitting for Vrot, Vrad, and ΔVsys; adjust centre, Vsys, PA, and inclination by hand to minimize ΔVsys and Vrad and match harmonic shapes.
key_parameters: Ring spacing: half-beam-width increments or at least 30 pixels per ring; fixed PA and inclination across all radii; 50 Monte Carlo trials varying centre by ±0.4'', PA by ±5 deg, inclination by ±4 deg
assumptions: Inclination and PA are fixed to a single value at all radii; no beam smearing correction applied; CO is dynamically cold (Vrot/σV > 4) and traces the total galaxy potential

recipe.goal: Derive stellar mass and stellar circular velocity profiles
recipe.method: Sum surface brightness in concentric annuli on Spitzer 4.5 μm (or PS1 r-band for NGC 5692) maps, convert to luminosity and mass using constant Υ*, and compute the stellar velocity curve using NEMO.
key_parameters: Annuli match CO radial binning inside CO extent and are 5 pixels wide beyond CO out to Rmax,*; Υ* = 0.21 ± 0.04 (4.5 μm) and 0.83 ± 0.15 (r-band)
assumptions: Stars are in a thin disk; constant mass-to-light ratio Υ*; maximal disk enforced where V* > VCO (first five bins in NGC 4701 and first bin in NGC 5692)

recipe.goal: Decompose dark matter density profile and measure inner slope (β* and β_1-2%Rvir)
recipe.method: Forward-modelling affine-invariant MCMC fitting a generalised NFW (gNFW) dark matter profile (plus stellar and gas components) to the CO rotation curve, computing β* (between 0.3 and 0.8 kpc) and β_1-2%Rvir at each MCMC step, and extrapolating total potential to estimate Rvir, M200, and c200.
key_parameters: 300 walkers, 300 steps, 100 burn-in steps discarded; initial values: ρo = 0.5 Msun pc^-3, rs = Rmax, β = 0.5; lookup table grid for PA (±5 deg) and inclination (±4 deg) in 1 deg steps
assumptions: gNFW dark matter density profile; independent Gaussian uncertainties on rotation curve points; H0 = 73.2 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 (ρcrit = 148.7 Msun kpc^-3, Rvir = R200); atomic/molecular gas negligible where unavailable

answer_key.quantity: Mean inner dark matter density slope <β*>

evidence.quote: We find $\langle\beta^*\rangle = 0.6$ with a standard deviation of $\pm0.1$ among the galaxies in this sample, in agreement with previous measurements in this mass range.

answer_key.quantity: Median of summed posterior distribution of β*

evidence.quote: The median of this distribution is $\tilde{\beta}^* = 0.5^{+0.4}_{-0.6}$, where the lower and upper uncertainties correspond to the 16$^{\rm th}$ and 84$^{\rm th}$ percentiles of the distribution (1-$\sigma$ for a Gaussian distribution).
